I am a qualified Primary Teacher, and I have been teaching since 2003. I have undertaken the duties of a class teacher, including safeguarding of children, following the National Curriculum to plan for all individual needs, deliver and assess lessons, and also to collect and interpret assessment data. This data contributed and assisted me to report (verbally and in writing) to parents and outside agencies. 

I also had responsibility for areas of curriculum (Music & Science). This role enabled me to encourage good working practices, to support and lead teachers in both subjects by planning, organising relevant meetings and training when necessary.

In 2019, I took on further responsibility as Key Stage 1 Lead, and within this leadership role I liaised with senior leaders; to ensure continuity and progression throughout the curriculum. The role also consisted of monitoring the quality of teaching and learning, in line with the school policy. This included lesson observations, monitoring of planning and scrutiny of pupils work across the school, and monitoring the standards of behaviour and achievement across the Key Stage.  

I take a lot of pride in my positive, considerate and cooperative relationship with staff, learners and parents, and these values have continued throughout my recent role as a Recovery Partner at St. Andrew’s Healthcare. Establishing this professional working relationships with patients and staff to promote REDS Recovery College initiatives is vitally important.

Working in education has also helped me to use my transferable skills to deliver recovery focused education to learners, including patients, medical students, staff and members of the community, to improve their knowledge and their own mental health and well-being. 

I use my own lived experience of mental illness, sharing my recovery journey and professional knowledge to inform training design, inspire hope, promote recovery-focused practice across the Charity and to support learners in their journey towards living a more hopeful and fulfilled life. 

I independently conduct research on new course topics, learning styles and modes of learning. Being able to use my vast experience in education and teaching skills has helped me to adapt delivery options and teaching styles to optimise accessibility, particularly within the charity’s Neuropsychiatry division. 

For pleasure and relaxation, I love to take regular walks with my dog, socialise with friends and family, listening to audiobooks. I have enjoyed fundraising for Northamptonshire Mind, Bliss and Cancer Research.

Having worked for Coca-Cola, Disney & Nike for 19 years, in varying roles: Retail Brand Director, Digital Sales Director, Trade Marketing Manager, Women’s Sales Manager, and latterly Sales Director for Running and Women’s. I started wondering… what was the world like outside of US mega brands? I never took my career for granted. I feel immensely lucky to have had the opportunity to learn and grow with these global power houses. I started to become “Curious”… “Curious” to know what the outside world could offer, “Curious” about pursuing my passions for consulting and teaching. I was “Curious” about the way in which large corporates do business. Having worked for three large US brands, I started to wonder if there was another way to do business, another way to build a business plan, understand a consumer, forecast. So the word “Curious” kept popping up. So when it came to creating a company it was right there in front of me… “Curious”.

I wanted to share my knowledge with others, work with different industries, partners, shaping their vision into a reality. This concept of enlightenment and questioning is converted into the multi-faceted approach of “Curious Consultancy.” A flexible, building block approach to grow your business, understand your consumer, build your retail estate, or for me to entertain and impart my wisdom onto you via keynote speaking and mentoring programs. If you’re interested? Have more questions than answers? The answer is in front of you, it just needs uncovering…

My vision for “Curious” – informed, modern, vibrant, humble.
